chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Muhammad al-Khazzaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one who publicises our Hadith to us, he is in the status of the one who denied us our right.
He said, and he said to Mu'alla ibn Khunays: 'The publiciser of our Hadith is like the denier of it'.

key_terms.أَذَاعَ: He publicised or made known widely
key_terms.حَقَّنَا: Our right (often referring to Wilayah or due authority)

ai.seo_question: What is the status of the one who publicises the Hadith of the Imams according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) equates the public dissemination of his traditions with the denial of his divine right (Haqq), a concept particularly emphasized in his address to Mu'alla ibn Khunays. This hadith underscores the critical importance of accurate transmission and the spiritual weight of representing the Imam's teachings, linking the act of 'publicising' directly to the theological stance of acceptance or rejection of Imamate. It serves as a warning against careless narration, suggesting that misrepresenting the Imam's words is tantamount to rejecting his authority.
